name: CCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Crowned in an 8-man single-elimination tournament at the fed's own "Explosion!!" pay-per-view (30 March 1997), won by Desmond Harrison, its first champion; X.Plosion took the belt from him at FanFest, beat him again in the Slamfest main event of 9 July 1997, and was still champion when the fed's own 1997 record breaks off. When CCW returned in the winter of 2000 the title stood vacant, and a new tournament was begun to fill it.

name: CCW International Championship
epitaph: "Boardwalk" Bradley Warden became CCW's first-ever International Champion by beating "The Bullet" Ricky Revolution, and was still recognized as champion when the fed's own surviving record breaks off.

name: CCW West Coast Championship
epitaph: "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz won this title at CCW's own "First Night" debut show (18 January 1997); by the fed's first RSPWF broadcast that July his brother "IQ" Ian Quartz held it instead, an unrecorded transition, and Ian was still champion when the surviving record breaks off.

name: CCW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Murder Inc. became CCW's first tag team champions by beating the Devestation Express, and were billed to defend the belts against Fire & Ice at the fed's own "Explosion!!" pay-per-view (30 March 1997). By the fed's first RSPWF broadcast that July, Fire & Ice held them, by a change no surviving document records. When CCW returned in 2001, its own cards called Fire & Ice the last CCW Tag Team Champions.
